speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Defence (a) what efforts have been taken to address mental health issues affecting national servicemen; and (b) what are the plans to strengthen mental health support in the Singapore Armed Forces.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Defence what are the recent steps taken by the Ministry to improve the mental health and well-being of (i) Full-time National Servicemen and (ii) Operationally Ready National Servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: This is in line with the increasing prevalence of mental health issues at the national level.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: The increase in professional expertise is necessary and the SAF will hire more if needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: But other measures are also needed to meet these rising demands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: The prevailing practice to screen for mental health issues among pre-enlistees continues, so that they can receive professional help and treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: For NSFs with mild and even moderate conditions but are assessed by our professionals to be able to serve in selected vocations, they will receive additional monitoring while in service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: These assessments and determinations are performed by our in-house professionals, guided by the advice of the SAF Psychiatry Specialist Advisory Board.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: This is an external panel comprising senior psychiatrists from our national healthcare system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: The SAF recognises that mental health issues can surface later, even when not picked up at pre-enlistment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: Therefore, we have increased our mental health support over the years, particularly during Basic Military Training, or BMT.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: These Care Hubs comprise medical doctors, psychologists, counsellors and orientation officers, working closely together with commanders to provide mental health support to servicemen during their transition into NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: Beyond self-help, our commanders interview BMT recruits regularly to identify potential problems and render assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: Training is provided to our commanders to recognise mental health issues and distress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: However, there may be recruits who are not comfortable to share their problems openly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: For that, there is an anonymous 24-hour SAF counselling hotline that they can call.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: NSFs detected with mental health conditions are closely monitored by a team of psychiatrists, psychologists, counsellors and medical officers during BMT and beyond.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: Our approach to mental health also includes prevention to promote mental well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: Well-being campaigns target both NSFs and Regulars to promote effective self-care, strengthen coping skills and better recognition of mental health issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: Reactions have been positive and service personnel are more open to discuss mental health issues and seek help.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: It consolidates our mental health professionals under one roof to better synergise and deliver care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: This office also works with the other Ministries and their efforts, which my colleagues have touched on at the Parliamentary Motion debate on advancing mental health on 7 February.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: We understand that mental health is a national challenge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: MINDEF recognises that we need soldiers who are both healthy physically and mentally for a strong defence.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Senior Minister of State, I take it that you are covering Question Nos 1 and 2?

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The reply is for Question Nos 1 and 2, Sir.
